cuts.raw_narration: In a quiet recovery room, Chairman Netero — an old bald man with a long white beard — sits beside Gon, a small spiky-haired boy whose right arm rests in a white sling. Netero holds up a plain plastic Hunter License and tells him, calmly, that what matters isn't how you become a Hunter, it's what you do with it. Gon stares back, still bandaged and processing, and repeats the words to himself: 'What I do, huh?'

Turning the conversation to the exam itself, Gon asks about the other applicants. Satotz, the exam proctor with the neat lavender hair and curled mustache, tells him the others are already in orientation. When Gon asks who wound up failing, the room goes still. Satotz answers softly: 'It was Killua.' Gon's eyes widen and he sits up. 'Killua failed? But why?'

To explain, Netero rewinds to what happened after Gon was knocked out. In the tournament hall, Killua — the white-haired boy in the dark turtleneck — stands facing an opponent whose long black hair falls straight past his shoulders. Long needles slide out of the stranger's scalp and his face reshapes itself. Killua goes rigid, staring at the blank-eyed man in the green tunic dotted with yellow spheres, and mutters that this is his older brother, Illumi. Illumi speaks first, evenly, as if greeting a coworker: 'I heard you stabbed Mom and Milluki.'

Illumi presses him — surely there's something Killua wants. Killua's composure finally cracks. He shouts back that there is: he wants to be friends with Gon, that he's sick of killing people, that he just wants to have fun for once. It's the loudest, most human he has looked all match. Illumi's face doesn't move. Flatly, almost bored, he tells Killua that friendship is impossible for him — he is incapable of it.

Then Illumi tightens the screw. He announces he'll simply go and kill Gon himself, and turns to walk out of the arena. When staff try to block him he brushes past. He stops and asks Killua point-blank whether he'll fight his own brother to save his friend. Killua's fists are clenched at his sides, his eyes trembling, but he can't move. Illumi answers for him: deep down, Killua isn't worried about Gon — he's worried about whether he can beat me.

On the sidelines Leorio and Kurapika are shouting for Killua to fight, promising to protect him. Illumi steps in close and rests one pale hand on top of Killua's head — Killua flinches, frozen — and in a small, defeated voice Killua says, 'You win, Illumi. I admit defeat.' Illumi lets go and smiles for the first time. He explains, mildly, that he was never actually going to kill Gon. It was only a test. And now he knows for certain: Killua is simply not qualified to make friends.

With Killua broken, the sixth match begins: Leorio, in his blue suit and round dark glasses, steps up against Bodoro, the older bald martial artist. Before Leorio can even settle into his stance, a blur cuts across the arena — Killua walks straight past him and strikes Bodoro down in a single motion. The referee stares, the crowd freezes, and Netero's voiceover confirms what everyone just saw: just like that, Killua killed Bodoro, and the committee disqualified him on the spot.

Back in the recovery room, Gon has heard the whole story. His jaw sets and his eyes narrow — Illumi trampled on Killua's one honest wish, the wish to be his friend, and pushed Killua into a place his brother could then use as proof. Gon is more than upset now. He is furious. He swings his legs off the bed, sling and all, and the scene lands on his face — no longer the wide-eyed boy from the opening of this story, but someone about to go after his friend.
